articles.title: Code Mode: the better way to use MCP
articles.why: This is the original post behind the Code Mode idea from your YouTube video. Instead of handing the model a pile of tools to call one at a time, Cloudflare turns MCP tools into a TypeScript API and lets the model write code against it in a sandbox, which cuts tokens and round trips. The follow-up posts and the REPL-style agent patterns you're seeing now all build on it.
articles.tryThis: Pick one multi-step chore you run with Claude Code (e.g. checking several job logs) and ask it to write one script that does all the steps, instead of calling tools step by step. Compare how long it takes and how much context it uses.
articles.pickReason: Starter pick — the post you mentioned tonight. Rate it to begin tuning.

articles.title: The components of agent memory
articles.why: Lance Martin lays out how Anthropic thinks about agent memory: fast capture during a session, then an offline 'dreaming' pass that checks notes against transcripts, builds linked wikis, and promotes the key notes into what loads at session start. It's the design thinking behind the memory features in tools like Claude Code, explained from the source rather than a summary.
articles.tryThis: Look at the CLAUDE.md in one Notice Conversion repo and trim it to what every session truly needs; move the rest into linked docs Claude can search, and tell it what memory is for instead of listing rigid rules.
